newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian call money ends easy, gilts slightly up.
newsitem.headline: Indian call money ends easy, gilts slightly up.

text.p: Indian call money ended down Monday at 3.25-3.5 percent on good liquidity while prices of government securities ended steady to marginally up, dealers said.
Most of the day's trade in call money was in a 3.5-3.75 percent range, dealers said.
Dealers said they expected call money to rise past 5.0 percent on Tuesday when banks make payments for bonds being auctioned today.
The Reserve Bank of India (RBI) auctions 50 billion rupees of four-year bonds later today and also holds a three-day repo auction of government securities.
"Call money rates will rise tomorrow as the outflows are fairly big," said a dealer at a foreign bank. "But I do not see rates going much above 6.0 percent."
"Liquidity is still good and nearly 45 billion rupees are locked up in repos with the RBI," he said. "How far rates go up will depend on how much is rolled over at the repo auction."
Dealers said prices of government securities ended steady to slightly up after a brief spurt in afternoon trade.
"A couple of foreign banks and an insurance company stepped into the market briefly in the afternoon," said a dealer. "This pushed prices up a bit but once they went off, the market slipped back."
"But for most of the day, trade was quiet....the market will take its clues from the bond auction results later today," he said.

The 12.59 percent 2004 stock ended at 105.0 rupees, off an intraday high of 105.08, against 104.95 on Saturday, the 12.14 percent 2000 at 104.30 against 104.27 and the 13.50 percent 1998 at 103.85 against 103.82.
Among other stocks the 11.83 percent 2003 rose to 102.05 from 101.90 and the 11 percent 2002 to 100.05 from 100.0
